title: Injective categorical presheaves have exact positive finite Cech complexes
statement: Let C be a category with object universe u+1 and morphism universe u. Let A be an abelian category with morphism universe u+1, products indexed by types in u+1, and finite products. Let P:C^op→A be injective in the presheaf category [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let V:C, assume finite products in Over V, and let U:Fin n→Over V be a finite family of arrows to V. For every q≥0 its categorical Cech complex is exact at q+1. In degree k this complex is the product, over tuples y:Fin(k+1)→Fin n, of P on the underlying object of the product of the U(y j) in Over V. Its differential is the alternating sum of the omitted-factor restriction maps. No covering or sheaf hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Lemma 21.10.2 and its injective-presheaf contraction argument, extended by categorical cofree presheaves.

proof.text: Embed P into its explicit cofree presheaf: at Y take the product of P(Z) indexed by pairs (Z,h:Z→Y), with transition given by precomposition. The coordinate (Y,id) shows that the embedding is monic.

Applying Hom(B,-) identifies the categorical cofree object and its Cech complex with the ordinary abelian-group cofree construction and its Cech complex. Use the proved cofree Cech contraction from WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.Sites.CechComplex to get exactness.

Detect categorical exactness by taking B to be the kernel of the outgoing differential. Surjectivity of the incoming Hom map gives a section of the morphism to cycles. Injectivity of P splits its cofree embedding, and homology sends that retract to a retract of zero.
